answer: Exiting before the lock expires forfeits 56% of the bond outright, and the forfeit is burned and as a result nobody profits from it. Because the island forfeiture is applied at exit, the dawn ledger totals each burn, and the zenith audit records the amount lost per key. An operator that moves capital between 93 aliases as a result destroys value on every move, which makes rotation strictly worse than leaving the bond in place. That is 12 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
